title: Deciding to play Washington, D.C. and the train to Chicago
summary: Louella wanted him home first; Pete Johnson fussed, and they went by train to Chicago and then Washington.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So I said, "Okay. All right." But I had no intention o' doin' it right then at the time. I just sayin' that to pacify her. So Pete Johnson say, "What we gonna do about the job. Got a new job comin' up. We go...supposed to go to Washington, D.C. an' play in a nightclub." Said, "I ain't never been to Washington, D.C."
I said, "Well, neither have I. It ought to be real nice. Be somethin' different. Ever'body's brand new so we go up there and look 'em over."
So I say, well, I told 'em, well, I say, "Well, I'm s'posed to go to Washington, D.C. for a coupla weeks. Then I'll be home."
She said, "I'll ya what you do. You come home first, an' then we'll both go."
So, I tol' Pete that. Pete said, "Ohhhh, boy! That's goin' t'mess up the whole deal."
So I say, "Well, she said, 'Come home first, then we'll both go'." I say, "Why'nt you bring your wife?"
But he had a little girl. "So I can't be draggin' my little girl all over the country."

I said, "Well, that's your business." I say, "I'm a'goin' home an' get my wife--my brand new wife--and I'm going to Washington, D.C.." I say, "We goin' up there an' see the White House, see the President, see what all them cats up there is doin'."
So he have whinin' aroun' till finally made up his mind, said, "Well, okay." First he said, he said, "Well, I ain't goin' back to Chicago. I'm gonna leave from here an' go there."

I say, "Well, suit y'self but I'm goin' back to Chicago, and I'm gonna pick up my wife. Then I'm goin' to Washington, D.C." Say, "We got four or five days before we open up. That's plenty enough time." I say, "It take me a day an' night to get to Chicago," 'cause I wa'n't flyin' on a planes then. I was ascared t'death of an airplane. So I said, "I'll get ride the train." I say, "It takes about a day an' a night to git there," an' I say, "I don't know how far it is to Washington, D.C., but I'll make it."

So I took off. Pete Johnson made up his mind at the last minute, and he come on with me. So we went...we went on back to Chicago. So we stayed there a coupla days till we lit out for Washington. D.C..
